records.title: A2 - Rick Wade - My Soul - Low Recordings
records.creator: 0x207b37ef59f53dbfcbf698ba58af9e2d7160ca01
records.note:
In this latest release, Rick delves into the depths of his soul to create a truly soulful sound. The EP opens with "Lonely Expedition," a track that begins with gentle yet poignant keys and expansive sounds, creating a sense of calm while building anticipation. As the track progresses, the smooth kick drums kick in, paving the way for the rest of the expedition with a familiar, heartwarming groove.

The following track, "My Soul," is a deeply evocative piece that features haunting vocals and captivating samples from classic films, all interwoven with a pulsating kick drum that underscores the profound journey of the soul. The EP comes to a close with "The Emperor," a steady ascent out of the soul with its ethereal beats, melancholic chords, and mellow baseline. The addition of a heartwarming sample from Charlie Chaplin's "The Great Dictator" adds a revitalizing touch to this beautiful and moving track.

Overall, Rick has delivered an exceptional EP that showcases his unique talents and creativity. The sounds of his soul are sure to captivate and delight listeners, leaving them feeling energized and inspired

Michigan-born Rick Wade might not get the headlines of his more celebrated Detroit peers, but few have done as much to contribute to the house canon as he. For nearly three decades, Wade has consistently turned out deeply channeled grooves, utilizing every second of their often-elongated lengths. Peppered lightly with strings, an odd breathy voice or some other delicate hook culled from the funk and soul sounds of his youth, Wade's style is the perfect embodiment of minimalist production delivering maximum impact.

records.title: Bull Run
records.creator: 0xece1917d248414cdfb27aee15d6a9bc3dd139c53
records.note:
The Brussels-based Algerian DJ and producer serves up five cuts of percussive club music inspired by traditional Berber music and British sound system culture. It’s a winning combo that will delight fans of the likes of DJ Plead, Toumba and the Livity Sound catalogue. It’s all deliciously minimal, with playful chirrups of bass, melody, and buoyant drums woven seamlessly around technoid pulses. From the lower tempos on display in ‘BubbleFly’, ‘Bull Run’ and ‘Smooth Jump’ to the nimbler flexes of ‘Baraka’ and ‘Siwtchover’, it’s an EP that displays the producer’s knack for subtly bubbling beats and mood-setting dancefloor NRG.

Words by EOIN MURRAY.

SC: soundcloud.com/kamounmusic

records.title: Kuskus
records.creator: 0x54e13f0060d9360807a805573f9734a097fb5542
records.note:
Kamoun has developed a signature sound where percussive intensity meets atmospheric depth, blending polyrhythmic drums with modern electronic textures. His fascination for traditional tribal percussion, paired with influences from minimalist field recordings and British bass culture, generates a hypnotic energy that resonates with the raw power of contemporary electronic music.
With the Artefact EP, Kamoun unveils three tracks exploring diverse sonic landscapes. Each piece stands out with its own identity, where rich vocals & textures and rhythmic complexity meet unexpected twists. There's something unpredictable that always surprises us that keeps the listener captivated from start to finish. 

Artwork:
Engraving by Iman Dubail

Sound:
Produced, composed and mixed by Kamoun (Abderrahmene Hamitouche).
Mastering by Hypna
Format - Digital - SKL010.

records.title: LOWRE02 - 4. Byron The Aquarius - Make Me Feel - Louder - Ten Eight Seven Mastered
records.creator: 0x207b37ef59f53dbfcbf698ba58af9e2d7160ca01
records.note:
Ah, Byron, Byron, Byron—what can we say? We're absolutely enamored with this guy's music. And, we couldn't be more thrilled to welcome him into our family on Low Recordings.

We are back with our second vinyl release, featuring Byron's "Love 4 Music." This 4-track EP is a celebration of love, with Side A and Side B showcasing two distinct styles where Byron truly shines. Side A delivers the club hits, while Side B envelops us in a soulful/R&B/deep house vibe.

Kicking off Side A is "Creepin' With U." The track begins with haunting chords that exude an eerie and raw vibe, swiftly leading into a thumping, club-certified kick drum. As the song progresses, a hint of nostalgia from the lo-fi days creeps in, complemented by vocal samples that add to the eerie atmosphere. Yes, it's eerie, but it's also robust and captivating—perfect for enticing bodies to move on a warehouse dance floor.

Next up is "Work That Girl (Tribal Mix)," the heavyweight of the four, tailor-made for the club/warehouse scene. The track starts with the clicking and clacking of hats and snares, Byron's vocals weaving in and out of the mix. The lyrics are crafted for a sweaty night of dancing, and as the kicks thump in, the energy rises. Byron's trademark chords seamlessly ooze into the mix, uniting our bodies with the song. Acid-sounding notes eventually lead us in and out of the groove—a solid club anthem.

Flipping over to Side B, we're greeted by "Inner Visions," where Byron slows things down and takes us in a different direction. A classic synth line initiates the track with a smooth kick, creating an airy vibe that melds perfectly with its melody. As the song grooves, Byron's soulful vocals pierce through, infusing warmth into his words. The warmth persists as the song progresses, with his voice echoing slightly more dissonance, leaving us with a proper vision for the closing track.

Closing out the EP, Byron guides us with a vision for a fun night in "Make Me Feel." Deep with a touch of R&B, the song exudes warmth and is all about feeling good with the person who got you through the night. Byron's sultry voice sits perfectly on the track as the basslines guide us through. His playful nature keeps things light and fun, rounding off the EP on a high note.

Artist Quotes:
Blessed Madonna
"Truly one of the greats doing work right now. Im grateful for this record. Thank you!”

Laurent Garnier
"Loooooove Byron's music”

Delano Smith
"Excellence in Deep House. Love all the tracks"

Kai Alce
"Byron always pushing forward!"

Louise Chen
"Everything I love is in this EP, deepness, rawness, escape and just beautifully crafted HOUSE!"

records.title: Lesbians on Mars
records.creator: 0xcbf418cf92ccced52422f94a4408111a8fafc0fc
records.note:
Seven months have slipped by. No sleep‑scribbled letters, no words from the Council. After releasing Vol. 1, I thought I’d feel relief, even freedom to make new stuff—but all I felt was a ghostly insistence—as if there were a chore I had to complete first, something I’d forgotten about. I began treating that absence as a puzzle. What was it trying to show me? I pride myself on keeping things tidy—yet like any producer, I keep a graveyard of musical ideas. While poking around my hard drive, I stumbled on a couple of tracks set aside during the making of A Spectral Turn. Could that be it? Maybe they were just waiting for their moment.

So, for Volume 2, I’ve gathered those pieces—some sketched in studio sessions three years ago, others composed for my live‑sets that followed the album release.

records.note:
"Healing Out Loud" is a groundbreaking musical experience from Heno. + Mad Keys that encourages listeners to confront their vulnerabilities and share their stories. This project redefines what it means to heal, grow, & connect with others by openly sharing the genuine truths of our human experiences. 

Heno. tells a story of personal growth, resilience, & the profound strength in embracing the scars that make us unique. Mad Keys provides a diverse sonic landscape with stylings tailored to amplify the emotions & stories shared by Heno. The project takes listeners on an introspective journey that's both personal & universal, fostering connection & understanding. 

This 10-track album is currently being mixed & mastered by Gregory Ebert, with creative direction from Karim Ali, content creation from Jamee Cornelia & features from MoRuf & Jaszy Shavers.

records.title: 8- Printemps
records.creator: 0x74585066d375a9bd5ca74e57ab71c640d30adb92
records.note:
Éditions Appærent and Pierre Guerineau are proud to present L’eau par la soif, their shared debut record.

Named after historical cases of mass hallucinations in French villages, Feu St-Antoine’s music reflects the subjectivity of reality, both as a personal and socio-political construct.

From the cold vocoder of “The Appærence” to the phased, swirling rhythms of “Spazio Libero,” or the vast, sprawling synth epics “L’eau par la soif” and “Printemps,” this record is immaculately rendered at every level; suffused with thoughts half-remembered, emotions never felt, and languages unlearned.

Language plays a crucial role here. Monologues and snatched phrases are buried in these tracks; one can even detect the cry and speech of Alex Zhang Hungtai’s slabbed, event-horizon saxophone. “L’eau par la soif” traverses the space between what is known and unknown, what is felt and unfelt, what is true and what is merely fact.

records.title: monkeypaw (original mix)
records.creator: 0xcbf418cf92ccced52422f94a4408111a8fafc0fc
records.note:
A few weeks ago, I woke up in bed to find a letter in my own handwriting

The Assembly of Many Names, duly convened and vested with authority across dimensions, hereby declares, as a matter of immutable principle, that tracks imbued with the memory of motion must not be confined or withheld. Such works, herein referred to as 'dance tracks,' are to spill freely into shadowed rooms, loud, unhindered and unbound. The practice of gatekeeping shall henceforth be abolished."

This could only mean one thing: it’s time to put together a new EP series. Starting with some tracks inspired by Tokyo's dancefloors I got to experience last summer. The next volumes will follow in their own time—every few months if I can keep up. I wouldn’t dare to challenge the Assembly.

records.title: A1. Zevar
records.creator: 0x2caaac33573292988f2d13081bb96c1a275c2ba1
records.note:
Spectral Bounce proudly presents Zevar, the debut release by Aedis, an alias of David Iriarte. This new undertaking sees the Amsterdam-based artist plumbing the depths & tunnelling further into a sound that has surely been in the works for some time. One half of Iro Aka, Iriarte is no stranger to the exploration of ambiance & rhythmic play: the duo released a trilogy of records on John Talabot’s label Hivern Discs between 2020 & 2023.

On Zevar, Iriarte first traverses the deeper territories of tech house before conjuring up mystic 2-step and delving into rolling techno. The sense of spaciousness throughout the EP is vivid: perpetually unfolding modulated delays; cavernous reverb; weighty, grounding sub frequencies. This expanse is punctuated by fragmentary voices, psychedelic refrains (“Xtz”), intricate break deployment (“Station”) and thudding bass tones (“RTHM”). Just enough is given, just enough held back. With these 4 tracks, Aedis brings you that little bit deeper.

Art by Susanne Janssen
Words by Cameron Leaf

records.title: A1. The Future Is Gone
records.creator: 0x2caaac33573292988f2d13081bb96c1a275c2ba1
records.note:
Spectral Bounce returns with a groovy and moody set of tracks by Uruguayan tastemaker Molen. 'Future is Gone' explores dark yet glistening corners of minimal tech house, blending distorted basslines, resonant synth leads, and muffled vocals to create a cinematic aesthetic.

Spectral Bounce’s third release continues to solidify the label’s sonic identity while opening avenues for artists to present their unique interpretations and perspectives, and Molen delivers on that promise.

Art by Susanne Janssen
Words by Hervé Kacou

records.title: A1. Dracula's MPC
records.creator: 0x2caaac33573292988f2d13081bb96c1a275c2ba1
records.note:
Reflex Blue debuts on Spectral Bounce with The Bleeps, a five-track EP that weaves a somber yet captivating late-night ambiance. Over a string of releases in recent years, Reflex Blue has been sculpting a distinct and evolving sound, blending the core minimal aesthetic of UK Tech House with influences from his homeland.

This homage to early 2000's Tech House captures its essence while infusing it with a fresh, pulsating perspective. The opening track, 'Dracula’s MPC', sets the tone with its club-ready elements: crisp drums, deep bass lines, and captivating vocal samples that command attention throughout. On the B-side, "Interlude" offers a glimpse into Reflex Blue’s large palette with its boppy and quirky breaks. It's a spectral record in every sense, making it the perfect sophomore release for the label.

Written and produced by Cooper Fraser
Artwork by Susanne Janssen
Words by Hervé Kacou

records.title: A1. Force of Nature
records.creator: 0x2caaac33573292988f2d13081bb96c1a275c2ba1
records.note:
Through their music curation work at One Eye Witness, co-founder Hylke has been silently influencing the sounds that resonate in clubs and underground dance music record collections around the world.

His newly created label Spectral Bounce takes it one step deeper, providing a platform for music imbued with eerie grooves and subtly expressive energy, capturing the listener right at their core.

SPEC01 - Force of Nature - Is the fruit of the long-standing musical relationship and shared visions of producer and Selector RDS and Spectral Bounce, the perfect catalogue opener.

Over four moody club-ready tracks, RDS dives into the sound of the after-hours, where minds are freed and darker energies are expressed. Both sides display perfectly controlled acid synthesis, heart-grabbing bass lines, cut-through drum sampling and an extremely textured and gritty mix. RDS' musical influences are clearly felt, harmoniously fusing UK 90s bleep techno, spacey tech house and dub with his own emotional perspective to club music.

The Dutch producer's distinct dance floor sound is here captured in its essence, processed through his expressive electronic machines while controlling tempo and energy in a unique manner. This EP is a sonic statement, offering the listener the Spectral Bounce sound.

Words by Hervé Kacou
Artwork & Logo by Susanne Janssen

records.title: MAPAGKEUN
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
DDR004 is "Mapagkeun Kawani," the debut 12" EP from Bandung’s own Xin Lie. This three-track offering skillfully combines the ethos of Bandung's hardcore punk scene with the evocative rhythms of Sundanese Dogdog drums, crafting a sound that is reflective of Xin Lie’s diverse musical background and connection to Indonesia's musical history.

Xin Lie, born Diannov Pamungkas, has navigated multiple worlds, starting from his days in the hardcore punk scene to exploring the traditional performing arts of his Sundanese heritage. This journey informs his approach to production, particularly his use of traditional percussion which he samples and recontextualizes into a modern electronic drum palette.

The EP includes two remixes: producer Bagvs delivers a sharp, stripped-down take on "MAPAGKEUN," while New York's Laenz transforms "PANEN" into a fast-paced, percussive wormhole.

All tracks written by Diannov Pamungkas
Mixing by Nahash / Raphael Valensi
Mastering by Enyang Ha / Urbiks

records.title: PANEN
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
DDR004 is "Mapagkeun Kawani," the debut 12" EP from Bandung’s own Xin Lie. This three-track offering skillfully combines the ethos of Bandung's hardcore punk scene with the evocative rhythms of Sundanese Dogdog drums, crafting a sound that is reflective of Xin Lie’s diverse musical background and connection to Indonesia's musical history.

Xin Lie, born Diannov Pamungkas, has navigated multiple worlds, starting from his days in the hardcore punk scene to exploring the traditional performing arts of his Sundanese heritage. This journey informs his approach to production, particularly his use of traditional percussion which he samples and recontextualizes into a modern electronic drum palette.

The EP includes two remixes: producer Bagvs delivers a sharp, stripped-down take on "MAPAGKEUN," while New York's Laenz transforms "PANEN" into a fast-paced, percussive wormhole.

All tracks written by Diannov Pamungkas
Mixing by Nahash / Raphael Valensi
Mastering by Enyang Ha / Urbiks
Artwork by Spaceheadtr

records.title: brain wash
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
The first installment in the Dance Data Lathe series comes from Munich-based, veteran producer Zero Crossing — with a remix from none other than trailblazing producer Shiken Hanzo.

Andreas Angerer, aka Zero Crossing, began creating his own music in the mid 90s. This release marks the return of the project via Dance Data and his first full EP since 2006.

'Brain Wash' dives into familiar yet sonically fresh territory, bringing the Zero Crossing sound full circle into 2024. Some listeners might initially draw comparisons to artists like Christoph De Babalon, Photek and even Shiken Hanzo himself — but they'll also notice a unique thread that is entirely Angerer's own.

Each song conveys a sense of isolation and being lost in an unfamiliar space — elements that, intentionally or not, bind the EP together. They traverse through a thick and ominous jungle, searching for a light in the darkness.

Then, Shiken Hanzo's interpretation of the track 'death fog' infuses it with a hyperdriven edge. He effortlessly blends elements from the original with rhythms and tones one wouldn't think possible — all the while building up steam for a head-swirling climax.

credits
All tracks produced by Zero Crossing
Mastered by Zero Crossing
Remix by Shiken Hanzo
Death Fog (Remix) mastered by Shiken Hanzo
Artwork by J. Pimenta

records.title: IELS
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
Preview only. 

ALBUM OUT APRIL 08 2025. 

We’re thrilled to welcome back Konalgad to Dance Data, this time with his debut LP, “Club Dream”. Spread across two discs for maximum fidelity, this is sound system music with grooves primed for mixing and dialed-to-a-Tee bass weight, but hovering above the grounded structures are fleeting rhythmic textures that veer things off into a world worth getting lost in. Throughout its 11 tracks, “Club Dream” plays out like a full mix, ebbing and flowing through a variety of energy levels and moods. Some of the range you’ll find here includes half-time dream-step, peak time pulses, and dubbed out mid-tempo tech, all done with a cohesive restraint and appreciation of atmosphere. The record imparts it’s own kind of dance floor dream logic onto the listener, inviting us to let go of making sense of things and trust in its fuzzy logic.

All tracks written and produced by Ahmad Qatramiz
Mastered by Alex Michalski

records.title: just tell me when you wanna ride
records.creator: 0x2793336c28def0a47f1fca2851b632362a6d4bfa
records.note:
"Rain from Heaven’s debut album, "petra-coeur", brings listeners into a vast liminal dreamspace between genres, one that is both pulsing with mystery and strangely familiar. Weaving together lush tapestries of guitar, gently danceable electro-acoustic beats, and warm ambient soundscapes, "petra-coeur" shimmers around Vazquez’s singularly nimble and yearning vocals, anchored all the while by an earthy post-grunge undercurrent. 

Nature, in all its forms and complexities, is the protagonist of "petra-coeur". Here, the digital and the organic blur into stunning new configurations, as Vazquez ruminates on urbanized indigeneity, ecological disaster, and love’s radical capacity for healing and regeneration. " -Kerosene Jones

records.title: Brote Extrano
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
We are incredibly excited and grateful to present 'NOCTURNO' - the first proper LP release by Chilean producer, Masot. The 10 tracks effortlessly traverse multiple genres throughout the album arc, showcasing a highly detailed and carefully designed sound palette - one which remains remarkably intact throughout the whole journey.

Moments of Nocturno feel melancholy and pensive, but never void of the hypnotic and percussive 2-step rhythms that feel like a darker take on the historically upbeat sound of UK 2-step and Garage.

Each song is meticulous, but not over-indulgent. The intricacy, melodic elements and club utility allow the LP to be as functional for the club as it is for at home listening.
credits
released May 25, 2024

All tracks written by Tomas Fernandez Quijada aka Masot
Mastering by CZ Wang
Artwork by Jesse Pimenta
Dance Data Digital (DDD003)

records.title: Citric Acid
records.creator: 0xf6b8d942ea953b625440fb0a3082352df34841bd
records.note:
This is a compilation of artists making electronic music outside of the cities which are historically renowned for dance music. Coming from Oklahoma City, we believe contemporary media should be accessible by anyone, regardless of where you live. All of these artists are indirectly connected through their drive to make something of where they live, not to try to make their hometown exactly like Berlin or New York. Instead, these artists take what is unique about their home-cities and amplify those idiosyncrasies to make something both rare and adventurous.


This is for them as well as anyone else living in a small town who wants to make dance music, throw raves, put out records, etc. We hope you reach out to people on this cassette. The night-time belongs to us, and we don’t have to dream alone.

records.title: over my head!
records.creator: 0x2793336c28def0a47f1fca2851b632362a6d4bfa
records.note:
"Rain from Heaven’s debut album, "petra-coeur", brings listeners into a vast liminal dreamspace between genres, one that is both pulsing with mystery and strangely familiar. Weaving together lush tapestries of guitar, gently danceable electro-acoustic beats, and warm ambient soundscapes, "petra-coeur" shimmers around Vazquez’s singularly nimble and yearning vocals, anchored all the while by an earthy post-grunge undercurrent. 

Nature, in all its forms and complexities, is the protagonist of "petra-coeur". Here, the digital and the organic blur into stunning new configurations, as Vazquez ruminates on urbanized indigeneity, ecological disaster, and love’s radical capacity for healing and regeneration. " -Kerosene Jones

records.title: Loisada Mama - skulptor
records.creator: 0x6519e6e1c353dbb3af20953caf93719777412b3a
records.note: Skulptor's first release of 2025 on CatalogWorks follows last year's successful single "FeltThat" with the same beguiling Latin Glitch Pop soundscaping they are known for. The difference is found in the distinct separation of both tracks, all written in Mexico City. "Loisada Mama" is a post-future dancefloor hit armed with uplifting chaos that's violently euphoric, driven by a projectile bullet beat. "W3theartz" (wet hearts), a homage to male tears, pivots into a sensual glitch-hop ballad armed with an unheard-of hook-bop that's both addictive and sweet. The EP features remixes from Bronx NYC's most prolific producer El Blanco Niño and Montreal-based slow-tech heavyweight SIM.

records.title: Adapting
records.creator: 0x4b185cee496d80ca7d66026d6f9fd9854823da97
records.note:
"Music is meant to be shared" - this is the defining ethos of pi pi pi, a multidimensional platform manifested for the music lovers, listeners, and dancers of our known universe. Whether it’s taking shape as a digital haven of music sharing, a conductive frequency of electrifying amusement, or a side quest with a friend in a lucid dream, pi pi pi has existed as an amorphous zone of (un)reality to inject some spritely silliness and funny fun back into the seriously serious seriousness too often found encroaching the joys of danceable electronic music.

True to its inquisitive nature and quest for fluidity, pi continues to evolve into new & enticing forms - this time, expanding it’s amoeba into a label and connective energy accumulator to bring forth Oscar Huang's debut EP "Slipstream". This first EP release for both pi & Oscar is a collection of tender dispatches recorded amidst the tumultuous landscape of the pandemic, but centered on motion and transcendence in spite of that.

records.title: Avuls I
records.creator: 0x53b247bc7b59f6ce6ee65faf0c1a263b1ac7e796
records.note:
Longstanding collaborators & Bay Area based experimental duo Kush Arora & Lucas Patzek aka Only Now & Orogen return with ‘AVULS’, the project’s sophomore release.
 
Building on the unearthly, black hole transmissions and creaking, exospheric ambience of their self-titled debut, Only Now & Orogen present an abyssal, elemental broadcast from another unchartered extra-terrestrial zone. Remote and astronomical yet tied to a newfound sense of rhythmic structure, ‘AVULS’ navigates a course through inverted beat-led frameworks, surging detonations of sub-bass, and severely turbulent, monumentally scaled soundscapes.
 
Amidst this large, slow-moving cyclone of sound sit fragmentary emergences of choral voices and Gregorian chants; a distant, esoteric presence within dense eruptions of attritional noise and infinite recesses of low end.
 
In harsh, pointillistic detail and through infernal surround sound, Only Now & Orogen channel dub, noise and power electronics, evoking a distorted, ritualistic inflection on the Voyager Golden Record; a mass of tectonic motion and friction; a storm in deep space.
Only Now is Kush Arora, Orogen is Lucas Patzek.
Mixed at Ancient Owl Audio, Berkeley, USA.
Mastered by Sam John at Precise Mastering, UK.
Artwork by Andrzej Masianis, Poland.
Recorded in Oakland, San Francisco, and Sonoma, California in 2019

records.title: Only Now x Dave Sharma - I Am Remembering
records.creator: 0x53b247bc7b59f6ce6ee65faf0c1a263b1ac7e796
records.note:
‘Timeslave (II)’ sees Kush Arora’s Only Now project return with renewed intensity, in the sequel to the formative Infinite Machine release ‘Timeslave (I)’.

After the groundbreaking hybridity of the debut volume in the ‘Indian Unclassical’ series, the emphatic riddim-focused explorations of dancehall, bashment, and drill found on the Club Yeke EP ‘Vision’ – released under Arora’s own name – and select live dates alongside the likes of Andy Stott, Debit & Nyege Nyege-affiliated metal pioneers Duma, ‘Timeslave (II)’ finds Arora invigorated by aesthetic variation and constructive collaboration.

Enlisting renowned, specialist percussionists including Iggor Cavalera (co-founding member of Sepultura), Dave Sharma (Sub Swara) & Ravish Momin aka Sunken Cages, Arora adds symbiotic fuel to the fire, infusing the resonant, largescale sound world of the Only Now project with raw, frenetic insurgencies of virtuosic instrumentation.

Set within devastating productions that venture into graphic drone, hyperkinetic drum sequences, dub ruination (‘I Am Remembering’), writhing, cataclysmic noise (‘Shiv – Vengeance 2’, ‘EVP Inversion’), and even, degraded, introspective doom metal interludes (‘Endless Defeat’), the restless rhythms of Arora’s collaborators add unprecedented dimensions to the resolutely dynamic material of the Only Now project.

Set within devastating productions that venture into graphic drone, hyperkinetic drum sequences, dub ruination (‘I Am Remembering’), writhing, cataclysmic noise (‘Shiv – Vengeance 2’, ‘EVP Inversion’), and even, degraded, introspective doom metal interludes (‘Endless Defeat’), the restless rhythms of Arora’s collaborators add unprecedented dimensions to the resolutely dynamic material of the Only Now project.

records.title: red light glow
records.creator: 0x2793336c28def0a47f1fca2851b632362a6d4bfa
records.note:
"Rain from Heaven’s debut album, "petra-coeur", brings listeners into a vast liminal dreamspace between genres, one that is both pulsing with mystery and strangely familiar. Weaving together lush tapestries of guitar, gently danceable electro-acoustic beats, and warm ambient soundscapes, "petra-coeur" shimmers around Vazquez’s singularly nimble and yearning vocals, anchored all the while by an earthy post-grunge undercurrent. 

Nature, in all its forms and complexities, is the protagonist of "petra-coeur". Here, the digital and the organic blur into stunning new configurations, as Vazquez ruminates on urbanized indigeneity, ecological disaster, and love’s radical capacity for healing and regeneration. " -Kerosene Jones

records.title: Winter hike
records.creator: 0xacd7c0361bbdf00244edd0cb7a9ae7959166fdf6
records.note: Hailing from Moscow and St. Petersburg respectively, Sergey Podluzhniy, Piper Spray and Lena Tzibizova come together as AIR Krew and share with us “Discuss and Come Back.” While floating broadly in post rock's orbit, the album charts a pretty unpredictable course from beginning to end, with an ornate sentimentality running as a constant from track to track. As in most cases, the words don’t do justice to the sound, the map really isn’t the terrain and you’re better off taking the time to explore it all for yourself.

records.title: Soft Fascination
records.creator: 0xebcc523f8f254f4775f191b699478994424663cd
records.note:
In the heart of Los Angeles' endless traffic buzz, a sonic collective emerged, championing the idea that higher BPM music need not be harsh or monotonous. Recently, their mantra, "Fast Not Hard," faced scrutiny: could it truly endure, or was it simply an idealistic phase?

Just as doubt peaked, an unexpected helicopter delivered a mysterious capsule, possibly from the future—or aliens. Inside was tangible proof of their philosophy: a sleek disc containing three original tracks that captured their ethos. Embraced as sacred scripture, it was named "Soft Fascination," embodying their nuanced approach. Group member Carré became their inaugural leader, charged with spreading this musical gospel.

Carré preached through "Soft Fascination," merging classic dubstep basslines with gentle melodies, gradually evolving toward accessible, rhythmic structures. "Glowing" highlighted simplicity and clear, spacious sounds, while "Cute Mad" radiated playful positivity and lively bass.

Before returning home to refine this ethos further, Carré recruited two distant disciples: Priori, who transformed "Soft Fascination" into an industrial soundscape, and James Bangura, who expanded "Glowing" into a profound, melancholic experience.

Thus, the "Fast At Work" movement solidified, its principles proven spiritually, musically, and physically. With Carré soon passing leadership onward, the future alone—or perhaps those enigmatic aliens—knows the true reach of their gospel.

records.title: Motion Therapy
records.creator: 0xebcc523f8f254f4775f191b699478994424663cd
records.note:
“Chop chop chop”—as the rhythmic reckoning approaches, we rave disciples remember the roots of our journey and its vibrant evolution. Past scripture recalls our beloved helicopter's arrival, delivering a sacred capsule from the future—or perhaps aliens—containing tangible proof of our enduring "FAST NOT HARD" belief. Yet, we understand all philosophies must evolve.

Thus, we celebrate the birth of the HOVER CAPSULE, a sub-disc expanding our sonic gospel through handpicked apostles, each illuminating distinct visions of musical ascendance. Side A presents foundational heli-dogma: first matriarch Carré teams with legendary phonic guru Addison Groove, joined by rising duo Baalti and London underground's Adam Curtain, crafting hymns of rhythmic unity. Side B dives deeper into emotional expressions of tempo. Ruby May Moon & Emanuel offer poetic intensity, while Introspekt elevates the message through dissonant two-step spirituality. Finally, Data Plan & 11:68PM encapsulate an ethos forever expanding—hovering gracefully forward.

records.title: 08 Populous - Exotic veneno
records.creator: 0xfce86fb693316a0123e86be545f7de3d5660be89
records.note:
“Isla Diferente” is the title of the new album by Apulian producer Andrea Mangia aka Populous. It’s the first release on his newly founded label, Latinambient, a name initially conceived to describe the sound of the album, which later evolved into a sonic manifesto and record label. 
All the tracks were written between January and February 2024 during an artistic residency in Lanzarote. “Isla Diferente” (Different Island) is the nickname of the most mysterious of the Canary Islands. A unique place, shaped by lunar landscapes, silent volcanoes, untouched nature, and art. Andrea spent a month at Hektor, a finca in Los Valles, in the heart of the island, surrounded only by hills, crops, and farm animals.
Lanzarote served as the backdrop for the creation of an album that seeks to explore its peculiarity through contrasts. Blending the ethereal sweetness of ambient music with the physicality of electronic and experimental latin rhythms, “Isla Diferente” attempts to capture the essence of an austere and wild place, where the lightness of the wind clashes with the hardness of imposing rocks, and where the white and green of the houses starkly contrast with the darkness of the volcanic soil. The album’s soundscapes evoke the vibrations of ecstatic dance, a movement that blends motion and transcendence through particular healing frequencies.

records.title: Scattered Cipher
records.creator: 0x0333c1fed26c4e8b76432945210de591bbc4c6a2
records.note:
H.D. Reliquary is the first eponymous release from Ben Shirken [a.k.a. Ex Wiish], and finds him returning home to 29 Speedway. The songs sparked during sessions with close collaborators - across 11 pieces, artists such as Pavel Milyakov, MIZU, Dorothy Carlos, Kevin Eichenberger and Muein breathe personality into the record. H.D.R. coaxes beauty from a serrated, raw, yet subdued palette drawn from improvised recordings of trumpet, violin, upright bass, cello, Max/MSP and modular synthesis.

The title references the hard drive as a sacred container for relics, contemplating how digitally archived fragments of one's existence can burn eternally after death. Archives, and in this case recordings, splinter and warp. Some distort what they contain. Some vanish, and others are eternally preserved, immune to deletion. Your information on these digital drives becomes archival shrapnel, the music that survives the remnants of collaboration.

Quick to note the dangers of creating music with ecologically intensive, mass marketed, and unethically trained AI software, Shirken employed bespoke, resource-light machine listening techniques for some of the compositional process. Pieces of recordings were fed into a series of proprietary neural networks, generating MIDI information and audio that reacted to on-the-fly soloing, imaginary sessions between players and algorithms invented posthumously.

Archives, and in this case recordings, splinter and warp. Some distort what they contain. Some vanish, and others are eternally preserved, immune to deletion. Your information on these digital drives becomes archival shrapnel, the music that survives the remnants of collaboration.

Quick to note the dangers of creating music with ecologically intensive, mass marketed, and unethically trained AI software, Shirken employed bespoke, resource-light machine listening techniques for some of the compositional process. Pieces of recordings were fed into a series of proprietary neural networks, generating MIDI information and audio that reacted to on-the-fly soloing, imaginary sessions between players and algorithms invented posthumously.

records.title: Threadline
records.creator: 0x03479c5f09817bf807798603d2cdf39c23127123
records.note: With Threadline & Rush, the third double single from The Songweaver, Merlin Modulaw delves into the project’s more synthetic and otherworldly side. These tracks are defined by icy, swirling synths, metallic drums, and fast-paced, trance-like melodies. The result is both haunting and euphoric—a soundscape that feels suspended between tension and release. The synthetic textures and driving rhythms create an almost hypnotic energy, while the melodies weave through the tracks like echoes from another realm. There’s a ghostly, untouchable quality to the sound, yet it retains an undeniable emotional pull. This release captures Modulaw’s ability to craft immersive electronic worlds that are at once coldly futuristic and deeply human, offering a glimpse into the darker, more frenetic side of The Songweaver.

records.note: Spectral Bounce’s fifth instalment comes courtesy of L.A.’s rave archivist and dancefloor operative Dreams, A.K.A. Jesse Pimenta. records.title: Meghnatis
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
Preview only. 

ALBUM OUT APRIL 08 2025. 

We’re thrilled to welcome back Konalgad to Dance Data, this time with his debut LP, “Club Dream”. Spread across two discs for maximum fidelity, this is sound system music with grooves primed for mixing and dialed-to-a-Tee bass weight, but hovering above the grounded structures are fleeting rhythmic textures that veer things off into a world worth getting lost in. Throughout its 11 tracks, “Club Dream” plays out like a full mix, ebbing and flowing through a variety of energy levels and moods. Some of the range you’ll find here includes half-time dream-step, peak time pulses, and dubbed out mid-tempo tech, all done with a cohesive restraint and appreciation of atmosphere. The record imparts it’s own kind of dance floor dream logic onto the listener, inviting us to let go of making sense of things and trust in its fuzzy logic.

records.title: A1 - نھایة إلى الطین : Ending Unto Dust
records.creator: 0x74585066d375a9bd5ca74e57ab71c640d30adb92
records.note:
The Tenets of Forgetting is the long-awaited follow-up to MSYLMA’s lauded 2019 debut, Dhil-un Taht Shajarat Al-Zaqum. This time he’s joined by fellow musician and producer ISMAEL for seven tracks, built around a lush palette of synths and MSYLMA’s singular voice.

Written and produced in Cairo between 2015 and 2020, The Tenets of Forgetting is the first collaboration between MSYLMA and ISMAEL. Like his first record, The Tenets of Forgetting finds MSYLMA singing in classical Arabic, and the musicians have enlisted Nariman Youssef to provide translations of the lyrics. This gesture of openness runs parallel to the themes of the record; romance and vulnerability; growth and change; pathos and passion. Listeners who aren’t familiar with pre-Islamic poetry or classical Arabic will find the lyrics just as rich and beautiful as the vocal melodies imply, telling a story of love, loss, self-doubt, and grave introspection.

Musically, the album moves in broad, painterly sweeps of 808 kicks, rich synthesizer chords, and MYSLMA’s soaring, plaintive voice. The English translations reveal a second world of mathematically sound rhythmic structures and poetry in the lyrics. The music pushes and pulls in both tempo and timbre, swirling both around and underneath MSYLMA’s voice but never losing a sense of self-contained narrative.

records.title: Contact
records.creator: 0x541c93695025df484d069b5e8481670b97df6da7
records.note:
Fortune Signal started as four friends with a shared obsession for dance music and a desire to carve out a niche that reflected our sensibilities. No big industry connects or main stage clout, just grit and passion. The shape of the label has always morphed to occupy the space where our individual tastes overlap. Three years, fifteen releases, and many late nights later, the edges of that shape have come into sharper focus. "Visions" is our clearest statement yet, and a signpost for where we’re headed.

These tracks represent our renewed musical vision for the future: discerning and contemporary production that sidesteps obvious tropes, restrained when it needs to be, powerful when it counts, a little off-kilter, but always with a firm grip on the groove. High-functioning club cuts from some of the most exciting producers in our orbit. "Visions" brings together new friends and old from our extended family across the US and UK. Some have released with us before. Some have played at our parties. Some are producers who we've been keeping an eye on and waiting for the stars to align. They're all artists we feel share our commitment to pushing forward-thinking dance music in a landscape that often defaults to the familiar.

records.title: dicotomiko
records.creator: 0x09e163e565cfc1662287c9125e96a3429a21bd1d
records.note:
*ESP**

'dicotomiko' nace como una respuesta a la persona que con rapidez llega a conclusiones y con deseos de representar, una figura ideológica que habla por el "pueblo"; genera retóricas y opiniones dicotómicas. Entendido como bueno o malo, si o no. 

Durante los últimos meses hice la reflexion siguiente. La expansion de pensamientos, cultura, & comunidad se forman mediante la integración, análisis, e intercambios de: las diferencias en opinion, y desacuerdos a travez de diálogos interpersonales. Me pregunto, como podemxs desarrollar colectivamente métodos para abordar el desacuerdo? Como minimizamos el lenguaje punitivo, y no acudimos al ostracismo social. 

Para que posicionarse como figura de 'salvador' que puede crear dinámicas de poder que establecen division y superioridad. También me cuestioné si rescatar raíces es algo malo. No es esta la vivencia de una multitud de migrantes y las generaciones que vienen? Si vuelvo al contexto en el cual se dieron estas opiniones, claramente habia intención de crear un ejemplo de lo que esta 'mal' y lo que esta 'bien' mediante un situación ajena a esa persona. Ahi si como dijeron por ahi, en la re mala, para aquellos que utilizan sus plataformas para generar discursos que separan, y promueven un ecosistema donde en muchas ocasiones es mas fácil lamerle el bon bon bum y quedarnxs en silencio que cuestionar. Admiro a aquelles que dicen algo que critican sin temor, me inspiran para también pararme y decir no me da miedo tener una opinion. Y le añado que sigo abierte al dialogo en lo que se pueda trankilitamente. Y que en verdad, pues tampoco es para decir, 'porque no le critican la opinion?' y juzgar el silencio de alguien a final si están de acuerdo pues también es valido o que cada quien tiene sus vivencias/razones.

Después de todo decidí acudir al regalo divino que me llego a la vida, para tratar de sacarme esa espinita que llevo por dentro. Con este tema expreso mis frustraciones, íras, enojos, decepciones. Intento expulsar ese sentimiento e intento a minimizarme y reducirme, indirecto o directo, que las acciones hablan. Para hacer juicios es importante que se sepa 'todo'. 

Desde el lanzamiento de mi proyecto sonoro y mi relación con a la musica procuro crear con mucho respeto desde un entendimiento de mis privilegios como persona que nace en un cuerpo de 'hombre' y con piel blanca miembre de la diaspora colombo-canadiense, y con una familia que me ha apoyado con mucho esfuerzo y trabajo. Para nada desconocido a el trabajo para sostener mi carrera como artista. 

Le entrego esta canción al universo y le pido a Dios que me ayude a dejar los rencores. Pa' que me saquen canas tampoco. Cierro con estas palabras.

El crecimiento colectivo depende de cada uno y la capacidad personal que tenemos para lidiar con conflictos entres todes. Por mas 'profesional' o 'laboral' que sean las cosas, quiero resaltar la importancia de observar la reacción y la acción. Cual nos permite aprender, y hablar? Así nxs tome un año en hablar para en conjunto encontrar soluciones y acuerdos que funcionen para cada persona afectada.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**ENG**

Dicotomiko is born as a response to those who quickly draw conclusions and aspire to represent an ideological figure speaking on behalf of the "people," generating dichotomous rhetoric and opinions. This perspective simplifies issues as either good or bad, yes or no.

In recent months, I’ve reflected on this: the expansion of thought, culture, and community is built through the integration, analysis, and exchange of differing opinions and disagreements via interpersonal dialogue. I ask myself: how can we collectively develop methods to address disagreement? How can we minimize punitive language and avoid resorting to social ostracism?

Why position oneself as a "saviour" figure, which risks creating power dynamics that establish division and superiority? I’ve also questioned whether reclaiming roots is a bad thing. Isn’t this the lived experience of countless migrants and the generations that follow? Reflecting on the context in which the previous was said, it’s clear there was an intention of making an example of what is “wrong” versus what is “right” using a situation unrelated to the person involved. As it was said, en la re mala (on the bad side), for those who use their platforms to foster divisive narratives and promote an ecosystem where, in many cases, it’s easier to stay silent than to question.

I admire those who dare to critique without fear; they inspire me to stand up and say I’m not afraid to have an opinion. However, I remain open to dialogue in a calm and peaceful way. And honestly, this isn’t about judging, “Why doesn’t anyone critique his opinion?” or judging someone’s silence. In the end, agreeing is also valid.

Ultimately, I decided to turn to the divine gift that came into my life to try and remove this thorn I was carrying. With this track, I express my frustrations, anger, disappointments, and rage. I tried to release these feelings that attempted to minimize whether directly or indirectly. To pass judgment, it’s crucial to know the full story.

Since launching my sonic project and exploring my relationship with music, I strive to create with deep respect, recognizing my privileges as someone born in a "man’s" body with white skin, as a member of the Colombian-Canadian diaspora, and as someone with a family that has supported me through hard work and effort. I am by no means unfamiliar with the work it takes to sustain an artistic career.

I offer this song to the universe and ask God to help me let go of resentment. No need for anyone to stress me out more than necessary. I’ll close with these words:

Collective growth depends on each individual and our personal capacity to handle conflicts among all of us. No matter how "professional" or "work-related" the issues may seem, I want to highlight the importance of observing both reaction and action. Which allows us to learn and generate dialogue?

records.title: Salt Pans - Julmud REMIX
records.creator: 0xa749c69856c787c38dacaef986255740996c4bfb
records.note:
Simsara Records commemorates Salute the Parrot’s 10-year anniversary with a remix compilation. Deena Abdelwahed, Noise Diva, El Waili, El Kontessa, Julmud, 3Phaz, and 3xOJ offer new takes on the album’s eight tracks. 

Surreal, stirring, and deeply rhythmic, Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan (Salute the Parrot) is just as raw and complex as the urban metropolis from which it came. The album’s impact runs so deep that it even helped shape the birth of Simsara Music, as founder Sarah El Miniawy’s experience listening to Louca’s album 10 years ago influenced her decision to focus only on music (and not other artforms) from the region. Simsara is now thrilled to present reinterpretations of this decade-old masterpiece, featuring the latest generation of boundary-pushing artists. The Salute the Parrot 10-year anniversary remix compilation comes out 28 Nov 2024 via Simsara Records. 

Louca recorded the album—his second full-length—during a momentous period in Cairo’s history. Amid political upheavals and increased access to the internet and social media, experimental artists emerged from the underground and started collaborating together for the first time. “Post-2011, it felt like a village,” Louca recalls. “You started looking and being inspired by people around you. Since then, most of my musical inspiration has come from the bigger family. Most of the records I’ve been listening to over the past ten years are records of friends.” 

While it’s steeped in the sounds of Cairo’s experimental and electronic scenes, Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan also draws on ideas from shaabi music—especially the Autotuned MCing style known as mahraganat, which exploded in popularity across Egypt at the same time that Louca was getting started on Benhayyi. Rather than rely on samples, Louca decided to make the album by going into the studio with the musicians around him. More than a dozen artists appeared on Salute the Parrot, contributing rebab, bouzouki, bass, drums, and Arabic keyboards. Mahraganat star Alaa 50 also provides vocals on three tracks. Back home, Louca moulded the recordings in post-production until he ended up with the final result. 

Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan (Salute the Parrot) opens with a slow fade-in. Mere whispers of a sticky synth groove grow in volume over a full minute until the tension finally breaks with the crash of a cymbal and the grand entrance of a psychedelic procession. Languorous keyboard ornamentations, a triumphant two-note riff, a snare drum so massive that it could crack a building’s foundation—all of it makes for a fitting start to one of the most epic albums to ever come out of Egypt. 

Through a swirl of maqam melodies and shaabi rhythms, Maurice Louca’s Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan bursts with vivid energy and shapeshifting ideas. The album earned widespread acclaim when it first came out on Nawa Recordings in 2014. It got accolades in critics’ reviews and year-end lists, and DJs bumped it over sound systems in venues from Beirut to Berlin. Louca kicked off a busy schedule of international tour dates for the first time, adapting the music for unique and hard-hitting live renderings. The title track appeared on the soundtrack to Leyla Bouzid’s award-winning 2015 feature film, A peine j'ouvre les yeux/As I Open My Eyes, and the music also inspired a younger generation of producers in the region to start making beats and rhymes of their own.

records.title: Ana 'Ishiqt (I Once Loved)
records.creator: 0xa749c69856c787c38dacaef986255740996c4bfb
records.note:
Two years in the making, Ahwar (Arabic for marshlands) is an otherworldly record, not unlike an abstract mythological story-tale. Opening with the mangled and filtered vocals of the album’s lead track Afqid Adh-Dhakira (I Lose Memory) like an alien dream, the drones of a bowed double bass lead us into a drum groove that lays the groundwork for El Shazly’s sultry and captivating presence, singing: "(I am) coming, from a time far away. Going, escaping. Alone in the wilderness". records.title: Mixing Colors
records.creator: 0x88b715c1063cdd3cb0aeccd7c7ac78e87f9f05b1
records.note:
Pulse is Qur'an Shaheed's debut for Leaving Records —as a pianist, poet, and vocalist from Pasadena, based in Inglewood— she fuses formal classical training with a deep commitment to improvisation. Guided by spurts of instinctual, jazzy vocalization and lyrics that incant dreams of an exalted future, Pulse transcends genre, capturing a journey toward presence, revelation, and a liberated poetics of sound. Through this album, Shaheed offers looping reflections on transformation and acceptance, revealing the fruitful arc of her artistic growth.

Shaheed's musical journey began in a family of musicians, led by her mother, Sharon, a pianist and music school owner, and her father, Nolan Shaheed, who toured with Stevie Wonder and was Marvin Gaye’s music director. records.note: In this track, a fluid fusion of World Jazz, Tunisian, and Electronic influences creates an entrancing experience that occasionally flirts with the experimental. The production shines with modern precision and organic textures, especially in the complex, rhythmically diverse beats infused with a jazzy oriental essence. The composition is elevated by a delicate melody, intertwining flute and violin, guiding listeners through a series of shifting atmospheres and breaks adorned with chill, atmospheric harmonies.

records.note: This EP offers a sophisticated fusion of global musical influences, North African rhythms, and contemporary electronic elements. records.title: ONOX68
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
The second entry on Dance Data is the debut album by Izapa, also known to some as Andrew Felix. Izapa has been a fixture in LA’s modular synth community for some time now, so it’s a treat to get a glimpse into the sounds he’s been honing in his private world.

The record showcases his sensibilities for a wide variety of rhythmic structures / styles, from angular hi-tek drum n bass to half time electro zoners, there is a little something for anyone that’s looking for dance music that prioritizes feel over function (while still retaining the latter). Featuring a swirling acidic remix from Buttechno.

records.title: XB098
records.creator: 0xed3acdd4669300eb2701466144866cd4ae520139
records.note:
The second entry on Dance Data is the debut album by Izapa, also known to some as Andrew Felix. Izapa has been a fixture in LA’s modular synth community for some time now, so it’s a treat to get a glimpse into the sounds he’s been honing in his private world.

The record showcases his sensibilities for a wide variety of rhythmic structures / styles, from angular hi-tek drum n bass to half time electro zoners, there is a little something for anyone that’s looking for dance music that prioritizes feel over function (while still retaining the latter). Featuring a swirling acidic remix from Buttechno.

records.title: Op Acid
records.creator: 0x9ee2dca90f4c2c60ac17458c9922b52ff57aaba4
records.note:
Part 6 of the Illegal Rave Tapes Series (1999-2012)

The Illegal Rave Tapes Series is a collection of solo electronic recordings by John Lee Richardson under the alias Acrelid.
Recorded at his Mum and Dads, and Hatcliffe House Studios between the years 1999-2012.

This series of solo electronic tracks, analog jams and experiments in Braindance/Techno/Jungle/Acid/Breakcore etc....whatever you want to call it....are the flipside to The Hatcliffe House Tapes Series. Recorded at the same time (some before) using the same equipment, in the same studio space.
Most of these recordings where made on cassette and mini disc reflecting the time period they was captured in and have been remastered, compiled and mixed for your listening pleasure.

records.title: thepawsarenotwhattheyseem
records.creator: 0xcbf418cf92ccced52422f94a4408111a8fafc0fc
records.note:
A few weeks ago, I woke up in bed to find a letter in my own handwriting

The Assembly of Many Names, duly convened and vested with authority across dimensions, hereby declares, as a matter of immutable principle, that tracks imbued with the memory of motion must not be confined or withheld. Such works, herein referred to as 'dance tracks,' are to spill freely into shadowed rooms, loud, unhindered and unbound. The practice of gatekeeping shall henceforth be abolished."

This could only mean one thing: it’s time to put together a new EP series. Starting with some tracks inspired by Tokyo's dancefloors I got to experience last summer. The next volumes will follow in their own time—every few months if I can keep up. I wouldn’t dare to challenge the Assembly.

records.title: Patina Shift
records.creator: 0x8524670e85c60d0f78da720c0de21e49be48d398
records.note: Corrosiv, the sophomore album from Orchestroll, reveals the duo at their most mature and vulnerable. Originally conceived as a reflection on hybridity and bastardization, the album deploys New Age and ambient compositional tropes as a launchpad, exposing their trite sanctity to the realities of corrosion. Having come of age in the 1970s and 1980s, the New Age movement perdures today as a domain of contradictions; its promise of transcendence riddled with the very commercialized dogma from which its adherents claim to flee. Healing modalities such as reiki, crystal therapy, and sound baths are simultaneously pathways to solace and sites of exploitation; their sonic counterparts — ethereal synth pads, shimmering textures, celestial drones — claim to facilitate meditation and enlightenment while devolving into empty signifiers of vitality. With Corrosiv, Orchestroll displays neither reverence nor disdain toward New Age: they exhume it instead, revealing the saccharine effervescence and commodified murk undergirding its aesthetics. The result is intoxicating — disquieting.

records.title: Null
records.creator: 0xfed2a9dcfd41dde8ef27fd100e014794a1e8322c
records.note:
A document of fleeting weight — WIN / LOSE inhabits the space between significance and silence. It traces the shape of connection in a collapsing frame, where presence feels like absence in slow motion.

Nothing here resolves. Nothing is claimed. Each moment flickers, then erodes — beauty appears, then forgets itself. It explores the fragile space where meaning slowly unravels through careless, fractured moments. It’s not about victory or defeat but the tension born from neglect, missteps, and the quiet decay that sloppy behavior leaves behind.

This is not a narrative of victory or failure. It is the tension between the two — the ache of holding meaning in a world that constantly unravels it.

It offers no conclusion. Only the echo of something that once mattered, and the quiet that follows.

Written, produced, and mixed by Diannov Pamungkas
Recorded by A (Soak) Vamp Dunning at XLNS
Mastered by Alikbal Rusyad at The Pandora Labs
Artwork by Kenny Reyhansyah

records.title: B1 - مذاهب النسيان : The Tenets of Forgetting
records.creator: 0x74585066d375a9bd5ca74e57ab71c640d30adb92
records.note:
The Tenets of Forgetting is the long-awaited follow-up to MSYLMA’s lauded 2019 debut, Dhil-un Taht Shajarat Al-Zaqum. This time he’s joined by fellow musician and producer ISMAEL for seven tracks, built around a lush palette of synths and MSYLMA’s singular voice.

Written and produced in Cairo between 2015 and 2020, The Tenets of Forgetting is the first collaboration between MSYLMA and ISMAEL. Like his first record, The Tenets of Forgetting finds MSYLMA singing in classical Arabic, and the musicians have enlisted Nariman Youssef to provide translations of the lyrics. This gesture of openness runs parallel to the themes of the record; romance and vulnerability; growth and change; pathos and passion. Listeners who aren’t familiar with pre-Islamic poetry or classical Arabic will find the lyrics just as rich and beautiful as the vocal melodies imply, telling a story of love, loss, self-doubt, and grave introspection.

Musically, the album moves in broad, painterly sweeps of 808 kicks, rich synthesizer chords, and MYSLMA’s soaring, plaintive voice. The English translations reveal a second world of mathematically sound rhythmic structures and poetry in the lyrics. The music pushes and pulls in both tempo and timbre, swirling both around and underneath MSYLMA’s voice but never losing a sense of self-contained narrative.

records.note:
The two of us have been working on music together for over two years, exploring new effects, timbres, and throwing anything we can at Ableton to see what sticks. These songs took shape as we applied our findings: field recordings of the wind and city, textured microsounds, recursive warping and resampling, and callbacks to our shared but distinct Chinese heritage.

records.title: HeartWerk - Plans That Never Pan Out - Low Recordings
records.creator: 0x207b37ef59f53dbfcbf698ba58af9e2d7160ca01
records.note:
Tulsa resident HeartWerk is hard at work in the state of Oklahoma spreading the soulful sounds of authentic house & techno to the masses. His excellent U Don’t Dance label which he uses as a platform for his music, in addition to others, has carved out a tight-knit community in Tulsa’s local electronic music scene and continues to do so with every release and party. HeartWerk now returns to the dynamic, LA-based collective and label, Low Recordings following their exquisite compilation that picked up an array of support from James Zabiela, Gene Farris, Nick Holder, Photonz, and many more.

‘There’s A New Cowboy In Town’ kicks off with sultry pads, fluttering melodies, and irresistible subs that draw you in instantly before ‘Plans That Never Pan Out’ lays down vibrant rhythms fused delicately with soul-infused leads and graceful bass that reverberates underneath. Up next, ‘Oklahoma Corral’ is a dreamy cut combining sparkling synths, infectious grooves, and divine atmospheres whilst ‘Printing Clouds Above Us’ displays organic field recordings that harmonies with soothing keys, and celestial ambiance. Rounding off the EP with pure energy is ‘Still In Love’, which focuses on effervescent, shuffling drums, resounding bass stabs, and rolling vocal samples.

records.creator: 0x207b37ef59f53dbfcbf698ba58af9e2d7160ca01
records.note:
Tulsa resident HeartWerk is hard at work in the state of Oklahoma spreading the soulful sounds of authentic house & techno to the masses. His excellent U Don’t Dance label which he uses as a platform for his music, in addition to others, has carved out a tight-knit community in Tulsa’s local electronic music scene and continues to do so with every release and party. HeartWerk now returns to the dynamic, LA-based collective and label, Low Recordings following their exquisite compilation that picked up an array of support from James Zabiela, Gene Farris, Nick Holder, Photonz, and many more.

‘There’s A New Cowboy In Town’ kicks off with sultry pads, fluttering melodies, and irresistible subs that draw you in instantly before ‘Plans That Never Pan Out’ lays down vibrant rhythms fused delicately with soul-infused leads and graceful bass that reverberates underneath. Up next, ‘Oklahoma Corral’ is a dreamy cut combining sparkling synths, infectious grooves, and divine atmospheres whilst ‘Printing Clouds Above Us’ displays organic field recordings that harmonies with soothing keys, and celestial ambiance. Rounding off the EP with pure energy is ‘Still In Love’, which focuses on effervescent, shuffling drums, resounding bass stabs, and rolling vocal samples.
credits

records.creator: 0x2e9cb4b101cdb9fabecfb6100802c4d91866e465
records.note:
Philo and dreadmaul first met at a festival in 2021 and immediately connected both on a personal and musical level. During the lockdown period, it was hard to meet in person, especially since they live in different cities. So they began working remotely, exchanging ideas online and visiting each other by time.

Their first result was the Do It Right EP on Defrostatica. But the collaboration continued and over time, the sessions evolved into something new: the Hotpants Kru EP inspired by the spirit of percussive Jungle-Techno and 90s gaming music in different tempi.

records.title: Walkin' Through That Door (feat. Feign Jima, Dylan Young)
records.creator: 0xcc19f902d3f7f004f796ff92c93bedf17df74b9f
records.note:
Winter McQuinn’s third record “Where Are We Now?” (out September 19th via Third Eye Stimuli Records & Born Losers) is the Melbourne/Naarm psych-folk and soft rock purveyor's most ambitious, collaborative and pop-leaning effort yet. Led by McQuinn, the 9 track album features co-writing and recording sessions with the likes of Dylan Young (Way Dynamic), Feign Jima, Hot Apple Band, Shelby De Fazio (Bad Bangs), Chet Sounds, Acacia Coates, GFS and Rudy Polacheck. The album continues the introspective and environmentally conscious lyricism that McQuinn has become known for, where he digs a little deeper inwards and ponders our existence and what it means to live a fulfilling life on this earth. McQuinn asks us to pause and consider; where are we heading?

Winter McQuinn recorded almost all of the record from his home studio in Northcote, Melbourne/Naarm. It was pieced together over two years (2023-2024) with McQuinn writing the bones of the instrumentals and then bringing in artists to write the vocals and melody together. Each song features a different vocalist, with McQuinn taking lead vocals on just two songs and it was also the first time that McQuinn wrote songs entirely on piano, which brought a new style to his songwriting. Mixed by Dylan Young (Way Dynamic, Cool Sounds, Good Morning) and Snowy (Good Morning, Snowy Band), the production is top tier and emphasises the warm, nostalgic pop tones of the album perfectly.

With McQuinn citing Carole King and Nick Drake as major influences on his work, his third record weaves vibrant soft rock, folk, country and psychedelic pop akin to contemporaries Kate Bollinger, Drugdealer and Alex Izenberg.

Where Winter McQuinn’s acclaimed 2024 record ‘Move To The Trees’ saw him bring together friends from Hot Apple Band and Sunfruits to perform the songs live in the studio, Where Are We Now? takes his collaborative nature to another level, breathing even more musical diversity and life into his songs. McQuinn wanted to bring together musicians he respects deeply and feels akin to stylistically, as he explains; “I wanted to do a project that involved a lot of the talented musicians and songwriters in my local community. It allowed me to follow any song direction or idea I had in mind and bounce ideas off of great musicians I’ve always wanted to work with.”

“Where Are We Now?” is a normal question to ask in a geographical sense, but when we tip into the philosophical world, we open a can of worms — a can that McQuinn is never afraid to open. His music is always pushing us to stop and think, to take a breath, to consider what we are doing, to be mindful of who we are as individuals, as a collective and where our future is heading. McQuinn explains; “on this record, the lyrics zoom in on a kind of introspective nature and ask questions or offer potential answers on what we actually need to be content in our lives and what that means to different people. There's also a lyrical focus on shared anxiety that I and a lot other people feel at the moment under this kind of environmental, neo fascist slow collapse. In that way it's definitely connected conceptually to my past two records (Move To The Trees, A Rabble Of Bees), but I think lyrically there's a lot more personal lines and it's a bit more pessimistic compared to my previous work .”

There’s a darkness within the songs but there’s always light too, with this record being focused around the idea of bringing like-minded people together, cherishing friendships and supporting musicians, to create something tangible and important, such as art. It’s through sharing ideas and creating together, that McQuinn and friends help weather the societal and digital shitstorm together.

records.title: Sebaas - Generative Chase
records.creator: 0xc0e1acebaba84aa8ce23e9849af788d1398cf418
records.note:
The Lossless Self EP is a two- track pack heavily influenced by dark and tribal sonic aesthetics. The output is a result of resampling organic drums, layered low ends, washed out highs, and a focus on telling simple yet concise rhythmic stories. 

The goal was to create juxtapositional compositions where there is a clear contrast between gritty/distorted elements and softer elements such as the synthesized pads in Generative Chase.

records.title: Sufi Dub
records.creator: 0x54e13f0060d9360807a805573f9734a097fb5542
records.note:
Kamoun has developed a signature sound where percussive intensity meets atmospheric depth, blending polyrhythmic drums with modern electronic textures. His fascination for traditional tribal percussion, paired with influences from minimalist field recordings and British bass culture, generates a hypnotic energy that resonates with the raw power of contemporary electronic music.

On 'Wave Prophecy', his first 12" on Dance Data, Kamoun showcases his distinct range - from deep tribal grooves to high-energy dance tracks, Kamoun fuses rhythmic complexity with avant-garde sensibility, forming a unique and addictive sonic palette.

As If the full 5 tracks weren't already enough of a treat, we've also got a fresh remix from our friend Sepehr, who takes La Panthère to a tantalizing place with his 'pantheress' rendition.

All tracks written by Abderrahmene Hamitouche
Mastered by Mark @ A Colourful Storm
Artwork by Jesse Pimenta
Remix by Sepehr

records.title: Beyond
records.creator: 0x0be352365ddbd69d09daed18ed27fd36a01207cd
records.note:
I flap my wings of imagination,
my aims set high,
to a place far beyond here.

But the weight on my shoulders grows,
as I push my tired self forward.

What lies there, I wonder?

This is a trial given to me.
A barrier I must break.
A rite of passage to a new world.

But I have stopped trying to break through it.
I simply decided to be here, with the familiar wall.

And then, for the first time, I saw it.
An unnamed flower at my feet, swaying in the wind.
Just as the flower finds peace simply by being,
so do I.

And here, I can finally breathe,
and feel the scent of a new beginning.

records.title: VitanovaV1.0
records.creator: 0xd7d1484539ea3c4e313bc0e9244276d58af82fdd
records.note:
The title Vita Nova comes from latin which means “new life”. It is the celebration of the coming of my first born son, Phoenix.
There are a couple of different moods which caracterise the piece, moving between and building on them. The first is the typical trippy, driving beat that builds up and establishes the psychedelic status quo. The other part, like a kind of chorus, is a more melodic and emotional space with some friendly aliens joining us in the mix later on.

Instruments: Silver Flute and Rhodes by Pearce van der Merwe
Tools: Logic Pro, Access Virus Snow
Written and produced by Flooting Grooves @ Starways Studio
Mastered by Mark Valsecchi @ Mixroom Studios
Visual Artwork by Gydravlik

records.title: RisenV1.0
records.creator: 0xd7d1484539ea3c4e313bc0e9244276d58af82fdd
records.note:
The slow groove, that emerges from the swampy depths of the earth, almost gives the illusion of stasis, but yet it moves forward in an ever-evolving storyline featuring alien conversation and nature, warped through the altered perception of the listener. Added layers of euphoria are delivered by the rhodes and the flute solos, the latter finally floating away on a sea of bliss.

Instruments: Silver Flute and Rhodes by Pearce van der Merwe
Tools: Logic Pro, Access Virus Snow
Written and produced by Flooting Grooves @ Starways Studio
Mastered by Mark Valsecchi @ Mixroom Studios

Visual Artwork by Jeremy Torman:
I created 2,000 psychedelic images with Stable Diffusion using a custom model trained on work by Eloh and myself. I then trained StyleGAN2 on those images, generated a music-synced animation, and finally processed each frame through the same custom Stable Diffusion model.
Frames were extracted post-production for the still images.

records.title: Sangre y Camino
records.creator: 0x94734e11b78680a35b0a86ba3ce634d334d6d2a7
records.note:
Inspired by inherited violence and the current social divisions in Colombian culture. Proposing a spiritual transformation based on the only truth: Jesus, as the Source of living water and our savior. And the transformation of consciousness through Music, Art and Disruptive Technologies. 

The work examines how forgiveness—both divine and human—can break cycles of violence and division that have plagued our society. The piece proposes that true transformation occurs not through retribution, but through the radical act of forgiveness modeled by Jesus Christ.

Sangre y Camino invites listeners into a space where personal and collective wounds can be transformed through divine grace and conscious choice.

/ Sonic Sacred Geometry /

Tuning: 432 Hertz Precise Temperament
Key: A minor
Bpm: 150
Country: Colombia
Year:2025
Produced, Mixed and Mastered by Yoshiro Mare

told in the silence between sounds.

The rhythm is found in what is not there.

records.title: Dogtown
records.creator: 0x680729c9d9555bcc4ec14670c7648d391263829c
records.note:
Back in 2021, I experimented with the sound of a glitching meditation cd. It turned into a lot more experiments with the manipulation of cd’s and mp3’s to create otherworldly sounds. The resulting album combines both meditative and jarring moments, like a computer’s intense dreams.

All music is composed, produced and mixed by Luuk van de Mosselaer. Huge thanks to Niels Adema, who played church organ on “Requiem for Audio Data Loss and Organ” in the Nicolaikerk in Utrecht. Artwork by Luuk van de Mosselaer.

Thanks to everyone who helped me think, gave feedback and listened to me ramble about a project that became a huge deal in my head.

All music is composed, produced and mixed by Luuk van de Mosselaer. Huge thanks to Niels Adema, who played church organ on “Requiem for Audio Data Loss and Organ” in the Nicolaikerk in Utrecht. Artwork by Luuk van de Mosselaer.

Thanks to everyone who helped me think, gave feedback and listened to me ramble about a project that became a huge deal in my head.

records.title: Idiot - Noise Diva feat. Krampfhaft REMIX
records.creator: 0xa749c69856c787c38dacaef986255740996c4bfb
records.note:
Simsara Records commemorates Salute the Parrot’s 10-year anniversary with a remix compilation. Deena Abdelwahed, Noise Diva, El Waili, El Kontessa, Julmud, 3Phaz, and 3xOJ offer new takes on the album’s eight tracks. 

Surreal, stirring, and deeply rhythmic, Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan (Salute the Parrot) is just as raw and complex as the urban metropolis from which it came. The album’s impact runs so deep that it even helped shape the birth of Simsara Music, as founder Sarah El Miniawy’s experience listening to Louca’s album 10 years ago influenced her decision to focus only on music (and not other artforms) from the region. Simsara is now thrilled to present reinterpretations of this decade-old masterpiece, featuring the latest generation of boundary-pushing artists. The Salute the Parrot 10-year anniversary remix compilation comes out 28 Nov 2024 via Simsara Records. 

Louca recorded the album—his second full-length—during a momentous period in Cairo’s history. Amid political upheavals and increased access to the internet and social media, experimental artists emerged from the underground and started collaborating together for the first time. “Post-2011, it felt like a village,” Louca recalls. “You started looking and being inspired by people around you. Since then, most of my musical inspiration has come from the bigger family. Most of the records I’ve been listening to over the past ten years are records of friends.” 

While it’s steeped in the sounds of Cairo’s experimental and electronic scenes, Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan also draws on ideas from shaabi music—especially the Autotuned MCing style known as mahraganat, which exploded in popularity across Egypt at the same time that Louca was getting started on Benhayyi. Rather than rely on samples, Louca decided to make the album by going into the studio with the musicians around him. More than a dozen artists appeared on Salute the Parrot, contributing rebab, bouzouki, bass, drums, and Arabic keyboards. Mahraganat star Alaa 50 also provides vocals on three tracks. Back home, Louca moulded the recordings in post-production until he ended up with the final result. 

Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan (Salute the Parrot) opens with a slow fade-in. Mere whispers of a sticky synth groove grow in volume over a full minute until the tension finally breaks with the crash of a cymbal and the grand entrance of a psychedelic procession. Languorous keyboard ornamentations, a triumphant two-note riff, a snare drum so massive that it could crack a building’s foundation—all of it makes for a fitting start to one of the most epic albums to ever come out of Egypt. 

Through a swirl of maqam melodies and shaabi rhythms, Maurice Louca’s Benhayyi Al-Baghbaghan bursts with vivid energy and shapeshifting ideas. The album earned widespread acclaim when it first came out on Nawa Recordings in 2014. It got accolades in critics’ reviews and year-end lists, and DJs bumped it over sound systems in venues from Beirut to Berlin. Louca kicked off a busy schedule of international tour dates for the first time, adapting the music for unique and hard-hitting live renderings. The title track appeared on the soundtrack to Leyla Bouzid’s award-winning 2015 feature film, A peine j'ouvre les yeux/As I Open My Eyes, and the music also inspired a younger generation of producers in the region to start making beats and rhymes of their own. 

Tracklist:
The Golden Age (Deena Abdelwahed REMIX)
Idiot (Noise Diva feat. Krampfhaft REMIX)
Salute The Parrot (El Waili REMIX)
Rupture (El Kontessa REMIX)
Salt Pans (Julmud REMIX)
It Will Set (3Phaz REMIX)
Spineless (3xOJ REMIX)

Original cover art photography Maha Maamoun
Cover art design Siko Tatour / Mooni Studio
Mastered by Kassian Troyer at Dubplates & Mastering
Rupture remix mixed by Okak Studio

My submission for the 1st #Catalogworks discord sample challenge (Sample stems provided by remcycles) - MAY 2022

I didn't start until 40 minutes before the playback stream for all the submissions was starting. miss you rem <3

Louca kicked off a busy schedule of international tour dates for the first time, adapting the music for unique and hard-hitting live renderings. The title track appeared on the soundtrack to Leyla Bouzid’s award-winning 2015 feature film, A peine j'ouvre les yeux/As I Open My Eyes, and the music also inspired a younger generation of producers in the region to start making beats and rhymes of their own.
